title: Knowledge asset
description: One knowledge asset as a single file. GENERATED from ontology/capabilities.ttl (version 0.2.0) by `python -m src.conformance.schema`. Edit the ontology, not this file.

$schema.description: Path or URL of this schema, for editors.

costPerEval.description: Order of magnitude, e.g. "1e-6 s", "10 s". Used to prefer among admissible operators.

deterministic.description: True for a degenerate kernel. Do not represent such a factor as a near-degenerate table.

drawKind.description: Joint: Returns joint draws across its output coordinates, preserving dependence. | Marginal: Per-coordinate marginals only. Using this where a joint is needed silently imposes independence.

items.description: BatchClassify: Classify many parent-state samples at once, e.g. a reference-state system reliability backend. | EvaluateDensity: p(target | given) pointwise. Required by density-based MCMC. | EvaluateLikelihood: L(given) = p(target = t | given) as a function of the parents. Required for backward messages. | NormalisingConstant: Can return Z. Needed where evidence probabilities are required; a sampler alone does not supply this. | SampleForward: Draw target given parent values. Required by forward simulation and IS proposals.

implementedBy.description: Wrapper location relative to the folder holding the declaration, as "file.py:ClassName"

parameters.description: The numbers themselves, in whatever structure the wrapper named by cap:implementedBy reads. This vocabulary fixes the contract around them, not their shape.

reproducible.description: Same output given the same seed.

serviceMetric.description: Service semantics used to select a system asset, e.g. travel-time. Sharing a target variable alone does not make simulators interchangeable.

source.description: Provenance of the numbers: citation, table, retrieval date, verification level. A folder asset keeps this in the SOURCE.md beside its asset.ttl; a single-file asset carries it here.

stateValues.description: Target states, in CPD column order. A list rather than repeated values, because the order is the content.
